head: Chrome zero-day: update Chrome now to fix a bug attackers already use
dek: Google released a Chrome update that fixes nine security flaws, including one that attackers are already exploiting. It's the eighth such Chrome zero-day this year.
details: The exploited flaw, CVE-2026-125350, is a use-after-free bug in Chrome's XML component, which can let an attacker corrupt data, crash the browser or run code. An anonymous researcher reported it on 6 November. Google hasn't said how it's being used. The fixed versions are 157.0.8103.50/.51 for Windows and Mac and 157.0.8103.50 for Linux. Other Chromium browsers such as Edge, Brave, Opera and Vivaldi should get the fix too.
where: Chrome on Windows, Mac and Linux
means: A website could use this bug against you until Chrome is updated.
todo: In Chrome, open the menu, go to Help > About Google Chrome and click Relaunch; update Edge, Brave or Opera when their fix arrives.
